en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered bird of prey endemic to the dense tropical forests of the island of Mindanao.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is a complex volcano featuring a main crater lake located within a larger caldera lake.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its marine biodiversity.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippines, containing the national capital region of Metro Manila.
The Philippine Sea is a marginal sea of the western Pacific Ocean, located east and north of the archipelago.
The tamaraw, or Mindoro dwarf buffalo, is a critically endangered bovine species found exclusively in the forests of Mindoro.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
The amihan, or northeast monsoon, brings cool and dry air to the Philippines from November to February annually.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest nickel reserves, primarily mined in the provinces of Surigao and Zambales.
